root_idea.summary: The root centers on darkness and analogous obscurity.
root_idea.development: Its semantic field extends from night becoming dark or being made dark to dim sight, obscured travel, and figurative feigning of blindness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَغْطَشَ.

senses.definition: To make the night dark; to darken it.
senses.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV, with the night as the object in the Quranic construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the night, to become dark.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use describing the night becoming dark.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer an eye-affection involving dim or weak sight and frequent tearing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of the eye or sight becoming dim and weak-sighted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter into or upon the darkness of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the plural construction أَغْطَشُوا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feign heedlessness or blindness toward a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feigned blindness may be visual or intellectual; the construction is used with عَنْ for the matter disregarded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Darkness, blackness, or confused obscurity of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One reported usage places it after غَبَشٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weakness or dimness of sight accompanied by frequent tearing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the eye-affection also described by غَطِشَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dark or trackless desert in which the routes are obscure and the right way cannot be found.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally in the expression فَلَاةٌ غَطْشَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dark, especially when applied to night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival epithet; related coordinated adjectival forms are treated as the same lexical branch.
Used as a personal epithet for someone affected by dim or weak sight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet denoting dim or weak sight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as an epithet applied to sight rather than as a general statement of night-darkening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who feigns blindness toward a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial adjective corresponding to تَغَاطَشَ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Darkness and confused obscurity of night.
Adjectival darkness and the sight-related epithet.

cautions: The Form IV Quranic use means causing the night to become dark; the related Form I intransitive use is kept separate.
The supplied transcription of Lane entry 29511 contains omitted coordinated Arabic around some alternative forms, so only the explicitly recoverable lexical branches are assigned.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: Some alternative coordinated headwords in Lane entry 29511 cannot be mapped with complete certainty because of transcription omissions; they are not promoted to separate meanings beyond the explicit dark-night, eye-affection, and sight-epithet branches.
